title: Crashes and performance, on web and native

fields.name: render_cause
fields.doc: Which kind of page failure a render_crashed record reports. Only render_error is a crash: chunk_reload is the page reloading itself after a failed lazy chunk.

fields.name: error_name
fields.doc: The caught error's constructor name, never its message. none means an error event whose error was null; a rejection is never none, and a non-Error reason is other.

fields.name: error_class
fields.doc: chunk_load when the message matches a lazy chunk-load failure, else other.

fields.name: error_fingerprint
fields.doc: First 12 hex of SHA-256 over the top 5 stack frames as file:line:col. Never the message or stack text.

fields.name: previous_client_session_id
fields.doc: The dead run's client session, as its run marker named it. Empty on a launch marker, which was written before JS minted a cs_.

fields.name: phase
fields.doc: How far the run got when the marker was last written: launch before JS ran, live once the call was up.

fields.name: visibility
fields.doc: The web page's visibility when the row was recorded.

fields.name: app_state
fields.doc: The native app's AppState when the row was recorded.

fields.name: clean_exit
fields.doc: The last clean exit the run marker saw: pagehide on web, call_ended on either platform. Absent means the run never exited cleanly.

fields.name: last_elapsed_ms
fields.doc: The dead run's outbox clock when it last wrote its marker: the last time it was provably alive.

fields.name: heap_used_mib
fields.doc: performance.memory usedJSHeapSize in MiB. Absent where the browser does not expose the heap.

fields.name: heap_limit_mib
fields.doc: performance.memory jsHeapSizeLimit in MiB. Absent where the browser does not expose the heap.

fields.name: heap_probe
fields.doc: Whether the heap numbers were measured. unsupported means performance.memory does not exist; it is never 0.

fields.name: memory_state
fields.doc: The run's memory reading for its window: web heap_probe mapped to measured/unsupported, native ActivityManager lowMemory to ok/low.

fields.name: js_ready
fields.doc: Whether the app's JS ran during the marked run. false on a launch marker written natively before React Native loaded.

fields.name: was_discarded
fields.doc: document.wasDiscarded of the run that found the marker: the browser discarded and restored this tab.

fields.name: pid
fields.doc: The dead native run's process id, as its marker wrote it.

fields.name: launch_id
fields.doc: The dead native run's launch id, minted by the native marker at process start.

fields.name: launched_at_ms
fields.doc: When the dead native run launched, on the device clock.

fields.name: will_terminate
fields.doc: Whether iOS fired willTerminateNotification for the dead run. The system also fires it when ending a running background app, so it never means the user closed the app.

fields.name: window_ms
fields.doc: How long the measurement window lasted.

fields.name: long_task_max_ms_30s
fields.doc: The longest main-thread long task in the 30 s heartbeat window.

fields.name: long_task_total_ms_30s
fields.doc: Total long-task time on the main thread in the 30 s heartbeat window.

fields.name: main_ping_max_ms_30s
fields.doc: The worker's ping to the main thread: the worst round-trip in the 30 s window.

fields.name: worker_late_max_ms_30s
fields.doc: How late the worker's own 1 s tick ran at its worst in the window: process or worker suspension, not main-thread work.

fields.name: js_lag_max_ms_30s
fields.doc: React Native: how late the JS 1 s interval ran at its worst in the window, the JS-thread stall.

fields.name: hidden_ms
fields.doc: How much of the missed heartbeat interval the page spent hidden.

fields.name: expected_ms
fields.doc: The heartbeat interval the timer asked for.

fields.name: actual_ms
fields.doc: The interval the timer actually got.

fields.name: probe_state
fields.doc: Whether the thermal or pressure probe could measure. unsupported means the OS or browser has no such probe; it is never 0 or healthy.

fields.name: thermal_state
fields.doc: The OS thermal state: iOS nominal/fair/serious/critical, Android light/moderate/severe/critical/emergency/shutdown. unsupported means no probe exists.

fields.name: cpu_pressure
fields.doc: The web PressureObserver cpu state. unsupported means the browser has no PressureObserver.

fields.name: exit_reason
fields.doc: Why the OS says the app last exited: Android ApplicationExitInfo reasons, iOS MX_CRASH for a MetricKit crash diagnostic, or the unavailability codes no_record, no_exit_reason and unsupported.

fields.name: close_reason
fields.doc: Why Sync closed the seat's websocket, as SocketClose.transport_reason names it.

fields.name: close_kind
fields.doc: The sync close's shape: a clean normal or server drain, or an abnormal transport end.

fields.name: close_code
fields.doc: The websocket close code the server sent, when one was sent.

fields.name: heartbeat_gap_ms
fields.doc: How long Sync had heard nothing from the seat when its socket closed.

fields.name: participant_id_hash
fields.doc: SHA-256 of the seat's participant id: how server rows name a seat without its id.

fields.name: socket_age_ms
fields.doc: How old the socket was when it closed.

fields.name: protocol
fields.doc: The sync wire protocol version of a socket row.

fields.name: sfu_outcome
fields.doc: How the SFU session ended, as the node records it.

fields.name: sfu_cause
fields.doc: The SFU node's close cause token.

fields.name: connected
fields.doc: Whether the media session ever connected.

fields.name: lifetime_ms
fields.doc: How long the media session lived.

fields.name: connection_id
fields.doc: The media connection (pm_) a session or DB row names.

fields.name: ended_at_ms
fields.doc: When a DB row says the thing ended, in epoch milliseconds.

fields.name: dead_markers
fields.doc: How many dead run markers the previous_run.read scan found and recorded.

fields.name: low_memory
fields.doc: Android ActivityManager.MemoryInfo.lowMemory at read time.

events.name: client.render_crashed
events.doc: The call UI failed: a React render threw, a lazy chunk reload, an uncaught error or rejection. The API logs the SDK's render_cause under the established cause log column on legacy rows; kernel rows carry render_cause. Message and stack text never leave the client, only error_name, error_class and error_fingerprint.

events.name: client.call_crashed
events.doc: The call crash fallback ('Something went wrong with the call.') was shown. shown is recorded only after the fallback commits and while it is visible, so a rendered fallback nobody could see never counts.

events.name: client.previous_run
events.doc: A run marker of a dead previous run, found by the next run's previous_run.read scan and sent under that run's credential. It describes the dead run, never the new seat: no pt_, ep_ or ten_ in the body. P0, because the next kill can take the marker too.

events.name: previous_run.read
events.doc: The once-per-boot scan of run markers of dead previous runs: ok when it scanned, expected(app.no_marker) when none were dead, error(app.storage_unreadable) when the marker store could not be read. Its record is also the proof the client could have reported a dead marker.

events.name: client.perf_heartbeat
events.doc: One 30 s window of the run's health: long tasks, worker-to-main ping, JS lag, heap and memory state, visibility or app_state. It is a window of evidence, not a claim of health: no heartbeats is a gap, never 'no stalls'.

events.name: client.timer_throttled
events.doc: The heartbeat worker's tick ran more than 45 s late: the tab or process was suspended, not merely busy. Slice 7 reads it for hidden-tab throttling.

events.name: client.app_js_fatal
events.doc: React Native's global error handler saw a fatal JS error: the app is about to die. Written synchronously to the native marker first, then recorded and flushed, then the previous handler runs.

events.name: client.memory_warning
events.doc: The OS warned the app about memory: iOS AppState memoryWarning, or Android lowMemory read on the heartbeat.

events.name: client.thermal_changed
events.doc: The OS or browser thermal/pressure probe's current state, emitted once at join and then on every change: iOS ProcessInfo.thermalState, Android PowerManager thermal status (API 29+), web PressureObserver cpu. probe_state=unsupported is itself the row, never absence.

events.name: client.app_exit_info
events.doc: What the OS says about the app's last exit: Android ApplicationExitInfo (API 30+, read once at launch for the marker's pid) or iOS MXCrashDiagnostic (iOS 15+). no_record means an empty exit list for that pid, no_exit_reason means the platform has no answer, unsupported means the API level can't ask.

events.name: sync.websocket.closed
events.doc: Sync's terminal log for the seat's websocket: the reason the socket closed, its kind, how long the heartbeat had been silent and which seat it was (participant_id_hash).

events.name: sfu.session.closed
events.doc: The SFU node's own outcome for the seat's media session: the same outcome the participant_media_sessions row saves, so the two are one witness of the close.

events.name: db.participant_media_sessions
events.doc: The checker's read of the seat's participant_media_sessions row: the node's own outcome, saved durably. Emitted by the evidence reader, never a program.

reasons.doc: The previous_run.read scan found no dead run marker: the last run left cleanly or this is the first.
The run-marker store (localStorage or the native file) could not be read, so a dead previous run may be unwitnessed.
The person ended the app themselves (swipe from recents, force-stop): REASON_USER_REQUESTED or REASON_USER_STOPPED.
The OS ended a launch that never ran JS for a reason that is not a crash: a background-started process the system reclaimed.
The whole process was paused: the worker froze as long as the main thread, which a main-thread bug cannot cause. Web only.

facts.name: page.render_crash
facts.doc: A page failure the seat's client reported. Claim: the render_cause; render_error and the unhandled causes are failures some finding must explain.

facts.name: page.crash_surface
facts.doc: The crash fallback the seat's client showed. Claim: the surface state; only `shown` proves the person saw it.

facts.name: perf.heartbeat
facts.doc: One 30 s health window the seat's client measured. Claim: the window's length; the measurement fields are in the value. Its delivery also proves this build can report slice 9 evidence, and its absence marks an open tail.

facts.name: perf.memory
facts.doc: A memory reading for the seat: the web heap probe's state on each heartbeat, or the OS memory warning. Claim: the memory reading (measured/unsupported/ok/low, or the warning's app_state).

facts.name: perf.thermal
facts.doc: The seat's OS or browser thermal/pressure probe state. Claim: whether the probe measured; unsupported is itself a reading, never absence.

facts.name: app.previous_run
facts.doc: A dead run's marker, reported by the next run under its own credential. Claim: the phase the dead run reached. The reporting seat's row names the dead cs_, which is what identifies whose run died.

facts.name: app.marker_scan
facts.doc: The boot-time scan for dead run markers. Claim: the op's outcome; ok or expected means the scan ran, error means it could not read the store. Its presence proves this client reports dead runs.

facts.name: app.js_fatal
facts.doc: A fatal JS error the native app recorded before dying. Claim: the error class; a fatal of class other is a failure some finding must explain.

facts.name: app.process_exit
facts.doc: What the OS says about a native run's end: the exit reason for a pid (Android) or a MetricKit crash (iOS). The rule compares it with the marker's clean_exit; the vocabularies differ (clean_exit vs REASON_*), so it is an event fact, not a once-fact disagreement pair.

facts.name: page.tab_close
facts.doc: Sync's close of a seat's websocket. Claim: the transport reason. It names the seat by participant_id_hash, which the rule resolves through the declaration.

facts.name: page.media_close
facts.doc: The media session's end for a seat, as the SFU node logged it and Postgres saved it: one outcome in two stores, so the rows share an origin and count as one witness.

symptoms.doc: The web call page threw during render and showed the crash fallback, including a lazy chunk that failed mid-call.
user_words: the page said something went wrong

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and name == 'client.perf_heartbeat'
witnesses.doc: The seat's health windows, which also prove this build reports slice 9 evidence and that the client stream covers the live span.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and (name == 'client.render_crashed' or (event == 'sdk.telemetry' and type == 'render_crashed'))
witnesses.doc: The crash the seat's client reported.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and name == 'client.call_crashed'
witnesses.doc: Whether the fallback was visibly shown; impact, never a second witness of the crash.

symptoms.doc: The browser tab died during a live call without pagehide (renderer crash, out of memory, tab killed while hung, discard), found on the next run from its run marker.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and name == 'previous_run.read'
witnesses.doc: The seat's scan for dead markers, which proves this client reports dead runs.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'sync.websocket.closed'
witnesses.doc: Sync's close of the dead seat's socket; the dead run cannot report its own end.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'client.previous_run'
witnesses.doc: The dead run's marker, reported by a later run of the same profile.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'sfu.session.closed'
witnesses.doc: The media session's end for the dead seat; the SFU row and its Postgres row are one witness.

symptoms.doc: An uncaught error or rejection hit the call page during a live call, and the page kept running.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and name == 'client.perf_heartbeat'
witnesses.doc: The seat's health windows, proving this build reports slice 9 evidence across the live span.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and (name == 'client.render_crashed' or (event == 'sdk.telemetry' and type == 'render_crashed'))
witnesses.doc: Uncaught errors and rejections the page reported and survived.

symptoms.doc: The native app died in the foreground during a live call: JS fatal, render error, native crash, ANR or foreground OOM kill.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and name == 'previous_run.read'
witnesses.doc: The seat's scan for dead markers, which proves this client reports dead runs.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'sync.websocket.closed'
witnesses.doc: Sync's close of the dead seat's socket.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'client.previous_run'
witnesses.doc: The dead run's marker.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'client.app_js_fatal'
witnesses.doc: A fatal JS error the dying run recorded itself.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'client.render_crashed'
witnesses.doc: A native render crash the dying run recorded itself.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'client.app_exit_info'
witnesses.doc: The OS's reason for the dead run's exit, plus the marker's own clean_exit claim for the same end.

symptoms.doc: The native app died at launch before its JS ran, found on a later launch from the launch marker.
user_words: the app dies when I open it

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where name == 'previous_run.read'
witnesses.doc: The reporting run's scan, which proves it reads launch markers.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where name == 'client.app_exit_info'
witnesses.doc: The OS's reason for the dead launch's exit; no reason is unknown, never healthy.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where name == 'client.previous_run'
witnesses.doc: The dead launch's marker: phase=launch, js_ready=false.

symptoms.doc: The OS or the user ended the native app while it was backgrounded or inactive during a live call.
user_words: the app died when I switched apps
I came back and the call was gone

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and name == 'previous_run.read'
witnesses.doc: The seat's scan for dead markers.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'sync.websocket.closed'
witnesses.doc: Sync's close of the dead seat's socket.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'client.previous_run'
witnesses.doc: The dead run's marker with its last app_state.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'client.app_exit_info'
witnesses.doc: The OS's reason for the dead run's exit.

symptoms.doc: The web main thread or the React Native JS thread was blocked for 1000 ms or more while the call was on screen.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and name == 'client.perf_heartbeat'
witnesses.doc: The seat's 30 s health windows. Missing windows are a gap, never 'no stalls'.

symptoms.doc: The web heap grew 300 MiB over baseline or reached 90% of its limit, or the OS reported low memory, during a live call.
user_words: the call got stuttery then died

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and (name == 'client.perf_heartbeat' or name == 'client.memory_warning')
witnesses.doc: The seat's memory readings: web heap probe state each heartbeat, native memory warnings.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and name == 'client.perf_heartbeat'
witnesses.doc: The seat's 30 s windows, which carry the heap numbers the baseline and growth test read.

symptoms.doc: The OS reported serious thermal state or CPU pressure for 60 s or more during a live call.
user_words: the phone got hot and choppy

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and name == 'client.thermal_changed'
witnesses.doc: The seat's thermal or CPU-pressure probe, emitted at join and on change; unsupported is itself a reading.
